quiz.about: Class 10 ICSE matrices — order, addition, subtraction, equality and scalar multiplication

questions.q: A matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns. What is its order?
questions.explanation: Order is written as rows × columns, so 2 rows and 3 columns give an order of 2 × 3.

questions.q: For A − B to be defined, the matrices A and B must have
questions.explanation: Subtraction (like addition) is only possible when both matrices have the same order, since it works element by element.

questions.q: If A = [5  8] and B = [2  3] (both 1 × 2), what is A − B?
questions.explanation: Subtract element by element: 5 − 2 = 3 and 8 − 3 = 5, giving [3  5].

questions.q: For a 2 × 2 matrix, if A = [[4, 1],[6, 2]] and B = [[1, 1],[2, 5]], the bottom-right entry of A − B is
questions.explanation: The bottom-right entries are 2 and 5, so 2 − 5 = −3.

questions.q: If [[x, 3],[4, y]] = [[7, 3],[4, 9]], then the values of x and y are
questions.explanation: Two matrices are equal only when every corresponding entry matches, so x = 7 and y = 9.
In scalar multiplication every entry is multiplied by 3: 3·2 = 6, 3·(−1) = −3, 3·0 = 0, 3·4 = 12.

questions.q: If A = [[9, 5],[7, 2]], what is A − A?
questions.explanation: Subtracting a matrix from itself makes every entry zero, giving the null (zero) matrix of the same order.

faq.q: When can two matrices be subtracted?
faq.a: Only when they have the same order, meaning the same number of rows and the same number of columns. You then subtract the entries in matching positions. If the orders differ, subtraction is simply not defined.

faq.q: How do you find the order of a matrix?
faq.a: Count the rows first, then the columns, and write it as rows × columns. A matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns has order 2 × 3, and it contains 2 × 3 = 6 elements in total.

faq.q: What does it mean for two matrices to be equal?
faq.a: They must have the same order and every pair of corresponding entries must be equal. This is why equal-matrix questions let you form equations like x = 7 or y = 9 by comparing entries one by one.

faq.q: How is scalar multiplication different from matrix subtraction?
faq.a: Scalar multiplication multiplies every single entry by the same number, so 3 times a matrix triples each element. Subtraction instead works between two matrices of the same order, taking the difference of matching entries.
